sources.entry: Harbor - Cloud native image registry that stores, signs, and scans content. (Source Code) Apache-2.0 Docker/K8S

summary.one_liner: Harbor is an open source cloud native container image registry that stores, signs, and scans images and Helm charts, extending Docker Distribution with access control, replication, and auditing.
summary.what_it_does: Harbor is a self-managed container registry for images and Helm charts, built on the open source Docker Distribution. It provides project-based role access control, so different users get different permissions per project. Policy-based replication can synchronize images and charts between registry instances using repository, tag, and label filters, with automatic retries on errors. It scans images for vulnerabilities and offers policy checks to block vulnerable images from being deployed. It also supports LDAP/AD and OIDC authentication, garbage collection to free space from deleted images, a web portal, audit logging, and a RESTful API with embedded Swagger UI.
use_cases: host a private container image registry
control which users can push or pull images per project
replicate container images between registries or datacenters
scan container images for vulnerabilities before deployment
integrate registry login with LDAP, AD, or OIDC single sign-on
run garbage collection to reclaim registry storage
how_to_run: Install Docker 20.10.10-ce+ and docker-compose 1.18.0+ on a Linux host
Download the Harbor release binaries from the releases page
Follow the Installation & Configuration Guide to install Harbor
To deploy on Kubernetes, use the Harbor Helm chart
notable: Extends Docker Distribution with access control, auditing, and management features
Policy-based replication with filters for repository, tag, and label
Release artifacts signed with Cosign, with a documented verification guide
Hosted by the Cloud Native Computing Foundation (CNCF)
Passed a third-party security audit by Cure53 in October 2019
caveats: The main branch may be unstable or broken; the README recommends using releases
Install requires Docker and docker-compose on a Linux host per the README system requirements
Some official Docker images include separate open source licensing terms (Photon OS)
keywords: share container images with my team
